executiveSummary: Two major earthquake crises dominate the global picture: western Colombia has reported at least 312 fatalities with roughly 29,000 homes destroyed and about 69,000 people affected or displaced. View Article On Indonesia's Flores Island, the death toll has risen to at least 71 with nearly 1,200 injured and over 59,600 people sheltering in tents and evacuation centers; reporting earlier in the week cited lower figures as assessments evolved. View Article Wildfires in British Columbia forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate, left about 2,200 still under evacuation orders, damaged or destroyed around 150 structures, and caused at least one death. View Article Severe flooding in Indiana killed at least seven people and prompted hundreds of evacuations, including of seniors in a mobile home community; the federal government approved disaster assistance. View Article Japan's Chiba prefecture experienced deadly flooding with at least five fatalities and around 400,000 residents under evacuation orders or warnings at one point. View Article Hawaii's recent tropical storm left one person dead, more than 100,000 customers without power at peak, and some communities isolated; most schools subsequently reopened as recovery advanced. View Article Puerto Rico initiated 48-hour rotating water shutoffs around the San Juan metro due to reservoir depletion from drought, affecting tens of thousands of residents. Source

outlook72h: Earthquakes (Colombia, Indonesia): Expect continued aftershocks and access challenges; prioritize debris clearance, WASH, emergency shelter scale-up, and MHPSS services. Flooding (US, Japan, India): Monitor for additional rainfall and riverine responses; prepare for localized evacuations, shelter extensions, and infrastructure safety inspections. Wildfires (Canada, US, Europe): Wind shifts could prompt rapid fire behavior and renewed evacuation orders; maintain ready-to-move shelter capacity and power restoration crews. Tropical impacts (Hawaii): Focus on road clearance, power restoration, and supply reach to isolated pockets; schools/critical services may open with contingencies. Drought (Puerto Rico): Anticipate extended rationing schedules; pre-position bottled water, hygiene kits, and health outreach for vulnerable populations.
regionalTrends: Seismic risk: Back-to-back mass-impact earthquakes (Colombia, Indonesia) with complex, evolving tallies indicate sustained aftershock and landslide exposure.
Hydrometeorological compounding: Flood emergencies from the US Midwest to Japan continue amid saturated soils and infrastructure vulnerabilities.
Fire weather: Prolonged heat and dryness sustain high wildfire potential in western North America and southern Europe despite localized containment gains.
Slow-onset stressors: Drought conditions (Puerto Rico) producing service rationing and secondary public health risks.
